title: Enzymatic pre-treatment with protease to reduce membrane fouling during ultrafiltration of fermentation broths

record.title: Enzymatic pre-treatment with protease to reduce membrane fouling during ultrafiltration of fermentation broths
record.abstract: Pre-treatment of a model fermentation broth (Bacillus subtilis cultivation medium containing 12 g/L total protein) with a commercial serine protease (Alcalase 2.4L, 0.05–0.5% v/v, 40–55 °C, pH 7.5–8.5) was evaluated as a fouling mitigation strategy prior to 30 kDa polyethersulphone ultrafiltration. Hydrolysis degree was measured by the OPA method and ranged from 8 to 24%. At a hydrolysis degree of 16%, the limiting flux increased by 38% compared with untreated broth, and the total fouling resistance measured at 2 bar TMP was reduced by 47%. Permeate protein content increased proportionally with hydrolysis degree, which presents a trade-off for downstream product recovery. Circular dichroism confirmed partial loss of secondary structure in treated fractions. The study demonstrates that controlled proteolytic pre-treatment can serve as a feasible upstream option for bioreactor clarification steps.
